oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Artificial Intelligence in the Editorial Process: Protecting Black Women and Girls, Scholarly Integrity, and Human Judgment
oai_dc:dc.dc:creator: Young, Jemimah
Farinde-Wu, Abiola
Johnson, Jennifer
Butler, Bettie
King, Natalie
oai_dc:dc.dc:subject: artificial intelligence
editorial ethics
peer review
Black women and girls
algorithmic bias
scholarly publishing
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping scholarly publishing and creating new opportunities and ethical challenges for editors, reviewers, authors, and publishers. This editorial establishes a framework for the responsible use of AI within the editorial process of the Journal of African American Women and Girls in Education (JAAWGE), with specific attention to initial editorial screening, peer review, and final editorial decision-making. We argue that AI may appropriately support selected administrative, organizational, and language-focused tasks but must not replace human scholarly judgment, compromise manuscript confidentiality, or become the basis for decisions concerning manuscript quality or publication. These concerns carry particular significance for JAAWGE because algorithmic systems can reproduce dominant epistemologies, racialized and gendered biases, and patterns of exclusion that have historically marginalized Black women, girls, and their scholarship. Drawing on emerging publication ethics guidance and scholarship on AI, peer review, and educational research, we propose a human-accountability framework grounded in confidentiality, transparency, evidence, fairness, intellectual independence, and responsibility to the communities represented within the JAAWGE scholarship.
